labeling_note: true_class and rationale were authored by reading each site's source context (file + surrounding lines) BEFORE running Girder on any site, per the frozen Stage 3 audit methodology. 'not_a_call_site' is a category this crude regex-based sampler could not avoid: enum-variant patterns/constructors, generic bound declarations, function definitions, doc-comment prose, macro_rules! definition bodies, commented-out code, and raw string literals that happen to contain call-like character sequences. These are published, not discarded, because the sampler's false-positive rate is itself part of an honest account of what a crude, Girder-independent site-selection method actually produces. confidence='medium' marks sites whose true class depends on a struct/trait field's declared type that was not visible in the sampled context window and was not independently re-verified against the full source; these are still best-effort judgments, not guesses, but carry more uncertainty than the 'high' confidence sites.
